title: Pope Francis Examination of Conscience
description: An examination inspired by Pope Francis' teachings on mercy, care for creation, family, social justice, and the joy of the Gospel.
source: Based on Pope Francis' Teachings and Writings

categories.title: Mercy and Compassion
categories.description: Reflecting on how we extend God's mercy to others, a central theme of Pope Francis' papacy.

items.text: Have I been quick to judge others rather than offering understanding and mercy?
items.clarification: Pope Francis: 'A little bit of mercy makes the world less cold and more just.'

items.text: Have I gossiped about others, damaging their reputation?
Have I held grudges instead of offering forgiveness?
Have I been indifferent to others' suffering, especially the marginalized?
Have I shown compassion to those who have made mistakes or are struggling?
Have I recognized my own need for God's mercy while being stringent with others?
Have I practiced the corporal and spiritual works of mercy in concrete ways?
Have I reached out to those who feel excluded from the Church or society?

categories.title: Care for Our Common Home
categories.description: Examining our stewardship of creation based on Laudato Si'.

items.text: Have I recognized the earth as a gift from God that requires my responsible stewardship?
items.clarification: Pope Francis in Laudato Si': 'The earth, our home, is beginning to look more and more like an immense pile of filth.'

items.text: Have I been wasteful of resources like food, water, or energy?
Have I made lifestyle choices that unnecessarily harm the environment?
Have I considered how my consumption affects the poor and future generations?
Have I taken concrete steps to reduce waste, pollution, and my carbon footprint?
Have I cultivated gratitude and wonder for God's creation?
Have I educated myself about environmental issues from a Catholic perspective?
Have I advocated for environmental justice, especially for poor communities most affected by environmental degradation?

categories.title: Option for the Poor
categories.description: Reflecting on our solidarity with and service to those in poverty.

items.text: Have I been indifferent to the plight of the poor and marginalized?
items.clarification: Pope Francis: 'The measure of the greatness of a society is found in the way it treats those most in need.'

items.text: Have I viewed the poor as objects of my charity rather than brothers and sisters with dignity?
Have I accumulated possessions excessively while others lack necessities?
Have I made the needs of the poor a priority in my charitable giving?
Have I advocated for just social structures that address the causes of poverty?
Have I recognized Christ in the face of the poor and suffering?
Have I invested time in personally serving and building relationships with the poor?
Have I simplified my lifestyle to share more generously with others?

categories.title: Family Life and Relationships
categories.description: Examining our faithfulness in family relationships, based on Amoris Laetitia.

items.text: Have I made time for my family, or have I allowed work or other activities to take priority?
items.clarification: Pope Francis in Amoris Laetitia: 'The welfare of the family is decisive for the future of the world.'

items.text: Have I been patient and kind with family members, especially when they make mistakes?
Have I expressed appreciation and gratitude to family members?
Have I brought prayer and faith discussions into family life?
Have I made our home a place of love, forgiveness, and understanding?
Have I been faithful to my marriage vows in thought and action?
As a parent, have I prioritized passing on the faith to my children through word and example?
Have I shown respect and care for elderly family members?
Have I worked to heal family conflicts through dialogue and forgiveness?

categories.title: Culture of Encounter
categories.description: Reflecting on how we build relationships and break down walls of division, based on Fratelli Tutti.

items.text: Have I closed myself off from people who are different from me in culture, politics, or beliefs?
items.clarification: Pope Francis in Fratelli Tutti: 'No one can experience the true beauty of life without relating to others.'

items.text: Have I made an effort to genuinely listen to and understand those with whom I disagree?
Have I allowed political or ideological differences to damage relationships?
Have I engaged in polarizing debates rather than dignified dialogue?
Have I dehumanized others or reduced them to a single aspect of their identity?
Have I worked to build bridges across religious, cultural, or social divisions?
Have I welcomed migrants and refugees as brothers and sisters?
Have I participated in or remained silent about nationalism, racism, or xenophobia?

categories.title: Digital World
categories.description: Examining our presence and behavior in the digital environment.

items.text: Have I used social media in ways that build up rather than tear down others?
items.clarification: Pope Francis: 'The digital world can be an environment rich in humanity, a network not of wires but of people.'

items.text: Have I spread misinformation, gossip, or falsehoods online?
Have I engaged in online arguments that damage dignity and unity?
Have I allowed digital devices to distract from present relationships and responsibilities?
Have I maintained appropriate boundaries with technology to protect family time and prayer?
Have I used digital tools to spread faith, hope, and love?
Have I fostered authentic connection rather than superficial online interaction?

categories.title: Joy of the Gospel
categories.description: Reflecting on our witness to the joy that comes from knowing Christ, based on Evangelii Gaudium.

items.text: Have I allowed worries, problems, or negativity to overshadow the joy of the Gospel?
items.clarification: Pope Francis in Evangelii Gaudium: 'The joy of the gospel fills the hearts and lives of all who encounter Jesus.'

items.text: Have I been a joyful witness to others of Christ's love and mercy?
Have I shared my faith with others when opportunities arise?
Have I allowed routine or complacency to diminish my enthusiasm for the Gospel?
Have I cultivated gratitude for God's gifts rather than focusing on what I lack?
Have I maintained hope and perseverance in difficult circumstances?
Have I allowed the Gospel to challenge my comfort and complacency?
Have I participated actively in the Church's mission of evangelization?

categories.title: Everyday Holiness
categories.description: Examining our lived holiness in ordinary circumstances, based on Gaudete et Exsultate.

items.text: Have I recognized God's call to holiness in my ordinary life and daily activities?
items.clarification: Pope Francis in Gaudete et Exsultate: 'We are all called to be holy by living our lives with love and by bearing witness in everything we do.'

items.text: Have I sought holiness in my specific state of life (as parent, spouse, single, religious, etc.)?
Have I avoided the extremes of intellectual pride or mere external observance in my spiritual life?
Have I practiced the Beatitudes as a path to holiness?
Have I incorporated prayer, Scripture, and sacraments into my daily life?
Have I been attentive to discerning God's will in daily decisions?
Have I accepted life's challenges and sufferings as opportunities for growth?
Have I sought to grow in the fruits of the Holy Spirit (love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, etc.)?
